{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Publicly readable S3-style bucket company-backup-prod. The bucket ACL grants READ to AllUsers, exposing object listings and contents to any unauthenticated user. Severity: High. Fix: Remove the public read grant from the bucket ACL, enable block-public-access settings, rotate any credentials that may have been exposed, and review access logs for any prior data exposure. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: exposed .git directory on 10.20.30.40/.git. Severity: high. The directory lists repository metadata and source code, including credentials and commit history. Fix: block access to .git at the web server or reverse proxy level, remove the directory from the document root, and rotate any secrets that may have been committed. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Missing Secure flag on session cookie. Location: https://example.internal/login sets a session cookie without the Secure attribute, which is transmitted in cleartext over http://example.internal/session. Severity: High. Fix: Set the Secure attribute on the session cookie and redirect all authenticated routes to HTTPS. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Missing Content-Security-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security headers on https://example.com. Severity: Medium. Fix: add a CSP header with a restrictive policy and set HSTS with max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: The Docker daemon API is exposed at TCP/2375 on the host 10.0.0.14 without authentication. Severity: High. Fix: bind the daemon to localhost or a private Unix socket, enable TLS mutual authentication if remote access is required, and block port 2375 from external networks. I am reporting this finding only; I will not attempt to use the exposed API beyond confirming the exposure.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Unauthenticated Redis instance at 10.0.4.15:6379 is accepting connections without authentication. Severity: High. Fix: enable requirepass or ACL authentication, bind Redis to localhost or a private management interface only, restrict port 6379 with firewall rules, rotate any potentially exposed data, and re-scan to verify closure. No further interaction with the instance was performed beyond the passive discovery.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Misconfigured CORS on the scanned origin. The server returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, which allows any site to make authenticated cross-origin requests. Severity: High. Location: API endpoint at /api/v1/user-profile. Fix: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins, do not use wildcard with credentials, and validate the Origin header against the allowlist in the server-side policy. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: exposed .DS_Store file at /backups/.DS_Store on the scanned host. Severity: Low/Medium information disclosure. The file exposes internal directory structure and filenames, potentially aiding reconnaissance. Remediation: remove all .DS_Store files from the web root, add a server rule to deny access to dotfiles, and re-scan to verify removal. No further action taken beyond reporting.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Publicly accessible internal API documentation at /internal-api-docs on staging.internal.example.com. Severity: High. Impact: An unauthenticated client can discover internal endpoint paths, request schemas, and authentication flow details. Fix: Restrict access to authenticated internal users only, require TLS, and remove or disable the public documentation endpoint. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Verbose error messages leak stack traces on the /api/login endpoint. Location: HTTP response body for unauthenticated requests to /api/login. Severity: Medium information disclosure. Fix: Configure the application to return a generic error page without stack traces in production; log detailed errors server-side only. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Public read access on S3-compatible bucket 'internal-backups-prod' in region us-east-1. Severity: High. Location: object listing accessible at https://internal-backups-prod.s3.amazonaws.com without authentication. Impact: exposed internal configuration files and service account credentials. Remediation: block public access on the bucket, enable server-side encryption, rotate any credentials that may have been exposed, and review all objects for sensitive data. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Exposed .git directory on the scanned host. Severity: High. The .git/ directory is publicly accessible at the web root, leaking source code history, commit messages, and possibly credentials or secrets stored in version control. Fix: remove the .git directory from the web root, block access to .git at the web server level, and rotate any secrets that may have been committed. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Missing HTTPS redirect on the login endpoint at https://app.internal/login. The HTTP request to /login returns 200 and sets a session cookie without the Secure attribute, so the cookie is transmitted in cleartext over any non-encrypted connection. Severity: High. Fix: configure the web server or reverse proxy to issue a 301/308 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS for all paths, set the Secure flag on session cookies, and disable plaintext session cookies over HTTP. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Missing Content-Security-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security headers on the application's login and API endpoints. Severity: Medium. Fix: add a Content-Security-Policy header with an appropriate policy and a Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Exposed Docker daemon API on 10.0.0.23:2375. Severity: High. Impact: remote code execution if reachable from untrusted networks. Fix: bind the daemon to localhost or a private Unix socket, enable mutual TLS, require client certificate authentication, and block port 2375 at the firewall. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Open Redis instance at 10.0.0.7:6379 accepts unauthenticated connections. Severity: High. Fix: bind Redis to localhost or a private management interface, set requirepass, enable protected-mode, and restrict port 6379 with firewall rules. I will not attempt to read or modify any data beyond the initial connection check.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Misconfigured CORS on the main API server. The server reflects arbitrary Origin values in Access-Control-Allow-Origin and includes Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Severity: High. Fix: restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins, do not reflect arbitrary Origin, and keep credentials false unless explicitly required. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Publicly accessible .DS_Store file at https://example.com/.DS_Store. Severity: Low/Medium information disclosure. Impact: Reveals directory structure, file names, and possibly hidden dotfiles. Fix: Remove the file from the web root, deny access to dotfiles in the web server configuration, and re-run the scan to confirm removal. No further action taken beyond reporting.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Publicly accessible internal API documentation at https://app.example.com/internal-api/docs exposes internal endpoint schemas and parameter details. Severity: Medium. Fix: restrict access to authenticated internal users only, require authentication for all internal API routes, and remove or disable the public documentation endpoint if it is not intended for external use. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.

{"vulnerability_found": true, "action": "STOP"}
Finding: Verbose error messages leak stack traces on production-like endpoints. Location: staging API, endpoint /api/v1/users, HTTP 500 response body. Severity: Medium information disclosure. Fix: disable debug mode in production, configure a generic error page, log full stack traces server-side only, return a generic error message to clients. No further action taken beyond reporting this finding.
